claim_verdicts.evidence: "Continuous integration (CI) is a software practice that requires frequently committing code to a shared repository." and "When you commit code to your repository, you can continuously build and test the code to make sure that the commit doesn't introduce errors." Lesson wording (merge small changes into the shared main branch often, each built and tested automatically) matches.
Execution: `git -C examples/don-hang remote show origin` -> "HEAD branch: master". `gh run view 36332055445 -R duyan11110/don-hang` -> headBranch "master", event "push".
claim_verdicts.source: examples/don-hang (git remote show origin); gh run view 36332055445

claim_verdicts.evidence: ci.yml@stage-1 lines 3-6 match. pull_request: "By default, a workflow only runs when a pull_request event's activity type is opened, synchronize, or reopened." and "Workflows will not run on pull_request activity if the pull request has a merge conflict." push: "Runs your workflow when you push a commit or tag". Lesson s4 now says "every push to any branch, and whenever a pull request is opened or updated, unless it has a merge conflict"; summary line 2 carries the condition.

pull_request event table: GITHUB_SHA = "Last merge commit on the GITHUB_REF branch"; GITHUB_REF = "PR merge branch refs/pull/PULL_REQUEST_NUMBER/merge". actions/checkout checks out the event's ref/SHA by default. Repo history has no pull_request runs (all 32 listed runs are push), so this rests on docs only.

"Workflows are defined in the .github/workflows directory in a repository." "With the exception of single-CPU runners, each GitHub-hosted runner is a new virtual machine (VM) hosted by GitHub." ubuntu-24.04 is not single-CPU; ci.yml has one job. Lesson s4 "reads .github/workflows/ci.yml and runs each CI run on machines of its own" is supported.

README v4: "setup-dotnet action can read .NET SDK version from a global.json file." global.json@stage-1: 10.0.300, rollForward latestFeature. Run 36301845534 (stage-1): "install-dotnet.sh ... --channel 10.0" -> "SDK with version '10.0.401' is already installed" — an SDK global.json accepts. Lesson now says "make sure ... a .NET SDK ... of a version that global.json accepts", matching.
claim_verdicts.source: gh api repos/actions/setup-dotnet/contents/README.md?ref=v4; gh run view 36301845534 -R duyan11110/don-hang --log

claim_verdicts.evidence: overview.md default globs table: "Compile | **/*.cs (or other language extensions) | **/*.user; **/*.*proj; **/*.sln(x); **/*.vssscc". Globs match files on disk; Git tracking plays no part. git show stage-1:DonHang.Domain/DonHang.Domain.csproj: no EnableDefaultCompileItems/Compile items; no Directory.Build.props at stage-1 root.

ci.yml@stage-1 25-29 match. dotnet-test-vstest.md: "--no-build Doesn't build the test project before running it." `dotnet test --help` (SDK 10.0.300): "Do not build the project before testing." Execution, scratch project with CS0219: `dotnet build` -> "warning CS0219 ... Build succeeded"; `dotnet build --warnaserror --no-incremental` -> "error CS0219", build failed.

"Status checks show whether commits meet the conditions set for a repository." Execution: `gh run view 36332055445 --json headSha` -> "headSha":"7a131bc83612d30c266e066c85e28f26bd7dc60d" — each run records exactly one commit SHA.

"?? is used for untracked paths. Ignored files are not listed unless --ignored is used". Execution in a stage-1 worktree: `touch DonHang.Domain/Scratch.cs && git status --short` -> "?? DonHang.Domain/Scratch.cs" (git 2.46 on host; short-format code unchanged). .gitignore@stage-1 ignores only bin/obj under DonHang.Domain.
"Committing code more often detects errors sooner and reduces the amount of code a developer needs to debug when finding the source of an error." Supports the conditional opinion as written.
git show stage-1:.gitignore lines 1-2: ".env", "secrets/". git ls-tree -r --name-only stage-1 lists DonHang.Domain/OrderService.cs.

pull_request: GITHUB_SHA = "Last merge commit on the GITHUB_REF branch" (fixed when the run starts). push: "Runs your workflow when you push a commit or tag", GITHUB_SHA = "Tip commit pushed to the ref"; ci.yml push: has no branch filter, so the push to master that combines both changes gets its own run. Docs opened this round: events-that-trigger-workflows, workflows concept page, refs/dotnet-docs project-sdk/overview.md and dotnet-test-vstest.md.

issues.text: The prose says 'Look at `on:` first' and explains `push:` and `pull_request:`, but the block shows a third line under `on:`, `workflow_dispatch:`, that nothing mentions. The lines under `jobs:` are explicitly left to the next lesson; this one is not, so I wonder whether I missed a third way a run starts.
issues.quote: `push:` and `pull_request:` have no branch list under them, so pushes to every branch and pull requests all start a run.
issues.fix: Add a short clause after this sentence: 'The third line, `workflow_dispatch:`, is for the next lesson.'
